In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chromatic number of random graphs with high minimum degree is almost surely equal to the choice number of random graphs.
the choice number is almost surely and at most for a graph G with minimum degree at most and no two distinct vertices having more than common neighbors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice number and the chromatic number of a graph are almost always determined by its minimum degree.

we show that the choice number (and the chromatic number), which can be much larger than the clique number, of a random graph G(n,p) is almost surely bounded by a constant times the clique number of G(n,p) plus a constant.
the chromatic number of a graph is bounded above by its choice number, and the choice number of a random or pseudo-random graph is bounded above (almost surely) by its maximum degree.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice number and chromatic number of a graph are not necessarily related.
the chromatic number of a graph is a robust property.
, in the context of random and pseudo-random graphs, the choice number can be controlled in a way that is impossible for the chromatic number.
